name: Roll a coin across your knuckles
description: Roll a coin across the knuckles of one hand so a watcher can see it travel.
l1c: Roll the coin from one knuckle to the next without dropping it.
l1d: You can move it one step.
l2c: Roll it across the row and catch it in the same hand.
l3c: Do it once while someone watches, and pick it up if it falls.
safety: Use a coin you may drop. Keep it away from mouths and from small children.

name: Catch a coin from the elbow
description: Place a coin on your elbow and catch it in the same hand.
l1c: Rest the coin on the bent elbow and show it is still.
l2c: Straighten the arm and catch the coin.
l3c: If you miss, show where it went and try once more.
safety: Use a soft space. Do not throw the coin at anyone.

name: Spin a pen and stop it
description: Spin a pen around your thumb and stop it in a writing grip.
l1c: Spin the pen once around the thumb.
l2c: Stop the pen in the hand, ready to write.
l3c: Write one word immediately after the stop.
safety: Use a capped pen. Do not spin it toward a face.

name: Send a yo-yo down and back
description: Send a yo-yo down and bring it back to your hand.
l1c: Let the yo-yo reach the end of the string.
l2c: Return it to the hand without the string knotting.
l3c: If it does not return, say whether the string or the throw failed.
safety: Use a yo-yo with a safe string. Keep clear of other people.

name: Land a ball in a cup
description: Swing a tethered ball into a cup and leave it there.
l1c: Show the cup and the ball on its string.
l2c: Swing the ball into the cup and stop.
l3c: Hold still so someone can see the ball stayed in.
safety: Use a light toy. Do not swing it at a person.

name: Spin a top and catch it
description: Spin a top and catch it while it is still turning, or let it spin out and say so.
l1c: Start the top on a flat surface.
l2c: Say when it is steady. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l2d: You can see a steady spin.
l3c: Catch it while it turns, or say it fell before you caught it.
l3d: You can end the spin honestly.
safety: Spin it on a clear table.

name: Balance a stick on a finger
description: Balance a light stick upright on one finger for a moment you can show.
l1c: Rest the stick and find where it stays.
l2c: Keep it up long enough for someone to see.
l3c: Take one step and say whether it stayed.
safety: Use a light stick, not a sharp point. Do not balance it over a face.

name: Pass a ball around your waist
description: Pass a ball around your waist and back to the start without a drop.
l1c: Move the ball around once.
l2c: Show the handoff behind your back.
l3c: Go back the other way once.
safety: Use a soft ball in an open space.

name: Juggle two balls in one hand
description: Keep two balls moving in one hand, separate from a three-ball pattern.
l1c: Throw one ball and catch it in the same hand.
l2c: Keep both balls moving in that hand.
l2d: You can run two in one hand.
l3c: Catch both and show the other hand was empty.
safety: Use soft balls. Juggle away from lamps and people.

name: Spring a deck between your hands
description: Spring a small deck from one hand to the other so the cards arrive in a stack.
l1c: Square a deck you may bend a little.
l2c: Release the cards so they travel to the other hand.
l3c: Square the cards and say if any fell.
safety: Use cards you may bend. Do not spring them at a face.

name: Palm a coin and show the hand
description: Hide a coin in the palm, show the hand as empty to a person you told, then produce the coin.
l1c: Place the coin so the palm holds it.
l2c: Show the hand, then bring the coin out.
l3c: Tell the watcher where it was.
safety: Do this only as a disclosed trick. Do not take anyone's money or pretend it is magic you refuse to explain to the person you are showing.

name: Hop a band between fingers
description: Move a rubber band from one pair of fingers to another with a hop the watcher can see.
l1c: Put the band on two fingers.
l2c: Move it to the other pair in one motion.
l3c: Repeat it slowly enough that someone sees the start and the end.
safety: Do not aim a stretched band at anyone.

name: Link two clips with a fold
description: Fold a strip so two paperclips link when you pull the ends, then show the fold.
l1c: Clip them on a strip in the setup you can redraw.
l2c: Pull the ends and show the clips linked, or say they did not.
l3c: Unfold a second strip and show where each clip sat.
safety: Use paper and clips. Do not present it as an accident.

name: Snap on both hands
description: Snap the fingers of each hand so another person can hear both snaps.
l1c: Make one audible snap. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l2c: Snap the other hand. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l3c: Snap once on each hand when someone points.
safety: Stop if a finger hurts.

name: Spin a plate on a stick
description: Spin a plate or a lightweight disc on a stick and keep it up for a moment.
l1c: Get the disc turning on the stick.
l2c: Keep it from falling for a moment a watcher can see.
l3c: Catch or lower it without a drop you ignore.
safety: Use an unbreakable disc in an open space.

name: Toss and catch a diabolo
description: Toss a diabolo up from the string and catch it on the string again.
l1c: Get the diabolo spinning on the string.
l2c: Toss it and catch it on the string.
l3c: Say whether it landed in the middle or ran to an end.
safety: Use a soft practice space. Keep the sticks away from faces.

name: Swing soft poi in one plane
description: Swing one soft poi in a flat circle beside your body.
l1c: Keep the circle next to the body, not across the face.
l2c: Change direction and keep the same plane.
l3c: Wrap or catch it against the body without a hit to the head.
safety: Use soft poi, not fire. Practice where you cannot hit someone.

name: Stack cups and unstack them
description: Stack three cups into a pyramid and take them down into a nested stack.
l1c: Stack three cups so each sits in place.
l2c: Take them down into one nested stack.
l3c: Do both parts and say which part you rushed.
safety: Use plastic cups. Do not stack where a fall hits a face.

name: Build a house of cards
description: Build a house of cards with a base and one story above it.
l1c: Stand two cards into one A-frame that stays.
l2c: Lay a flat card and add one frame above, or stop and say the base moved.
l2d: You can try a second story.
l3c: If it falls, point to the card that went first.
l3d: You can see the weak point.
safety: Use cards on a steady table, away from a fan or an open window.

name: Run a short domino line
description: Stand a short line of dominoes so tipping the first tips the last.
l1c: Stand at least six dominoes with a gap you chose.
l2c: Tip the first and show the last fell, or say where it stopped.
l3c: Reset the gap that failed and run that part again.
safety: Use dominoes or blocks. Keep them off the floor where someone walks.

name: Skip a stone once
description: Throw a stone so it touches the water more than once, or say the water was wrong for it.
l1c: Pick a flat stone and say why.
l2c: Throw it low and say how many touches you saw.
l3c: Say what you will not claim if you saw only one touch.
safety: Throw only where skipping is allowed. Do not throw toward people, birds, or boats.

name: Walk heel to toe on a line
description: Walk a straight line with the heel touching the toe of the other foot.
l1c: Walk the line once with heel touching toe.
l2c: Look forward for two steps and stay on the line.
l3c: Turn at the end and come back.
l3d: You can turn on the line.
safety: Use a line on flat ground. Stop if you feel unsteady.

name: Write with the other hand
description: Write your name with the hand you do not usually write with, so it can be read.
l1c: Write the name once. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l2c: Ask someone to read it, or read it yourself and mark a letter that failed.
l3c: Write one more word at the same size.
l3d: You can go beyond the name.
safety: Use paper. Stop if the hand cramps.

name: Read a line upside down
description: Read a printed line that is upside down to you, without turning the page.
l1c: Read one line aloud while it stays upside down.
l2c: Point to a word someone names.
l3c: Turn the page and correct any word you missed.
safety: Use a page you may handle.

name: Mirror-write your name
description: Write your name so it reads correctly in a mirror.
l1c: Write the mirrored name.
l2c: Hold it to a mirror and read it.
l3c: Rewrite one letter that failed the mirror.
safety: Use a mirror you will not drop.

name: Say a tongue twister cleanly
description: Say a short tongue twister through once without a stumble you ignore.
l1c: Say it once at a pace you can finish.
l2c: Say it once at a speaking pace and stop if you stumble.
l2d: You can attempt a clean pass.
l3c: If you stumble, mark the sound that caught you.
l3d: You can find the hard sound.
safety: Stop if it hurts your jaw. Do not mock someone's speech.

name: Beatbox a kick and a snare
description: Make two different mouth sounds, one for a kick and one for a snare, and alternate them.
l1c: Make one low sound and name it the kick.
l2c: Make a different sound and name it the snare.
l3c: Alternate them so a listener can point to each.
safety: Keep the volume kind. Do not record someone else.

name: Whistle a two-note signal
description: Whistle two different notes as a signal and have someone copy the order.
l1c: Whistle a high one and a low one.
l2c: Repeat them in one order you chose.
l3c: Ask someone to copy the order and say whether they matched it.
safety: Do not whistle loudly in a quiet place that asks for silence.

name: Play a note on a blade of grass
description: Make one tone with a blade of grass or a leaf held to the lips.
l1c: Produce one tone. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l2c: Change how you hold it and say what the tone did.
l3c: Stop and drop the grass where you may.
safety: Use a clean fallen blade. Do not use a plant you cannot touch safely. Do not share the blade.

name: Blow across a bottle
description: Blow across a bottle mouth and change the note by changing the water.
l1c: Produce one note on an empty or partly filled bottle.
l2c: Add or pour out water and say whether the note moved.
l3c: Play two notes in an order you announced.
safety: Use a bottle you may drink from later only if you keep it clean. Do not share a mouthpiece.

name: Make a hand shadow someone can name
description: Make a hand shadow and ask someone to name the animal or object before you tell them.
l1c: Cast one shape on a wall.
l2c: Ask what they see before you say the name.
l3c: If they cannot tell, change one finger and ask again.
safety: Use a lamp, not a flame. Do not shine it in eyes.

name: Clap a round with a partner
description: Clap a short pattern, then have a partner start it while you continue.
l1c: Clap a pattern of a few hits.
l2c: Have them start when you are still going.
l3c: Agree a stop and both stop there.
safety: Keep it quiet enough for the room.

name: Drum a pattern on your chest
description: Tap a three-hit pattern on your chest and repeat it once the same way.
l1c: Tap three hits you can remember.
l2c: Repeat it once without adding a hit.
l3c: Tap the same pattern on the table and say what changed.
safety: Tap gently.

name: Fold a paper hat that stays
description: Fold a paper hat and wear it long enough to turn your head.
l1c: Fold a hat from newspaper or a large sheet.
l2c: Put it on and turn your head.
l3c: If it slips, refold one edge and try again.
safety: Use paper, not a plastic bag.

name: Fold a boat and float it
description: Fold a paper boat and show whether it floats for a moment.
l1c: Fold a boat that sits open.
l2c: Set it on water and say if it floats.
l3c: If it sinks, point to where the water entered.
safety: Use a basin, not a deep or fast body of water.

name: Fold a fortune teller and use it
description: Fold a paper fortune teller, write four outcomes, and use it once as a game.
l1c: Fold the teller so it opens both ways.
l2c: Write four harmless outcomes.
l3c: Run it once with a person and read the outcome you land on.
safety: Do not write an insult. This is a paper game, not a prediction.

name: Fold a letter into itself
description: Fold a written sheet so the writing is inside and the sheet stays closed.
l1c: Write one line you will hide.
l2c: Fold it so the line is inside and the sheet holds.
l3c: Open it, show the line, and close it again.
safety: Do not mail it as a practice on someone else's address.

name: Fold a map to one panel
description: Fold a paper map so the part you need stays visible and the rest stays folded.
l1c: Point to the part you need.
l2c: Fold so that part is on top.
l3c: Open it and fold back to the same panel.
l3d: You can return to the panel.
safety: Use a map you may fold. Do not fold a fragile original.

name: Cut a symmetric snowflake
description: Fold and cut a paper snowflake that opens into a matching pattern.
l1c: Fold the paper into matching layers.
l2c: Cut a small shape and open it.
l3c: Point to one shape that repeats, or say where the fold slipped.
safety: Cut away from fingers.

name: Make a pinwheel that spins
description: Make a paper pinwheel and show it spinning when you blow or walk.
l1c: Pin or fasten the pinwheel so it can turn.
l2c: Blow or walk and show it turn.
l3c: If it does not turn, point to the part that catches.
safety: Use a soft fastener. Do not use a sharp pin toward a hand.

name: Stand a card triangle
description: Slot or lean cards into a triangle that stands, then set a light object on it or say it will not hold one.
l1c: Make one standing triangle.
l2c: Set a light coin on it or say it sags.
l3c: Point to the joint that held or failed.
safety: Use cards or light card. Do not stand on it.

name: Fold a fan that opens
description: Fold a paper fan and open it with one hand.
l1c: Make pleats that stack. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l2c: Open the fan in one motion.
l3c: Close it back into the stack.
safety: Use paper. Do not flick it at a face.

name: Make a paper spring
description: Fold or cut a paper spring that stretches and returns.
l1c: Make a spring from paper.
l2c: Stretch it and let it return, or say it tore.
l3c: Hang a light clip on it and say whether it held.
safety: Do not put it near a face when it snaps back.

name: Make a pop-up fold
description: Make one pop-up fold inside a card so a tab stands when the card opens.
l1c: Make one tab in the fold.
l2c: Open it and show the tab standing.
l3c: Close the card flat again.
safety: Use card you may cut. Cut away from fingers.

name: Cut a paper loop and say what you get
description: Make a paper loop with a half twist, cut along it, and say what happened.
l1c: Make a loop with one half twist and mark the twist.
l2c: Cut along the middle. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l3c: Say whether you have one loop or two, and whether you predicted it.
safety: Cut paper only, away from fingers. Do not claim a result you did not get.

name: Flex a hexaflexagon
description: Fold a simple flexagon and flex it so a new face shows.
l1c: Fold the strip into the flexagon.
l2c: Flex it until another face is on top.
l3c: Point to the face that was hidden.
l3d: You can find the new face.
safety: Use scrap paper.

name: Read a Roman numeral date
description: Read a year written in Roman numerals and write it in ordinary digits.
l1c: Point to each numeral you know.
l2c: Write the year in digits.
l3c: Point to a pair such as IV or IX and say what it does, or say the date has none.
l3d: You can read a subtractive pair.
safety: Do not invent a numeral that is not written.

name: Count on one hand in binary
description: Show the numbers from zero to five with finger positions you can explain.
l1c: Show two different positions and name them.
l2c: Show each number and say the fingers you used.
l3c: Let someone set a position you taught and say the number.
safety: Stop if a finger hurts. This is a finger code, not a claim about how computers work beyond the positions.

name: Tap a word in Morse
description: Tap a short word in Morse from a chart you can see, then check it against the chart.
l1c: Choose a word of three or four letters.
l2c: Tap the letters from the chart, with a gap between letters.
l2d: You can tap from the chart.
l3c: Point back to the chart and correct one mistap, or say it matched.
safety: Use a chart you can see. Do not send a distress signal as a joke.

name: Finger-spell your name
description: Finger-spell your name from a chart, slowly enough to be followed.
l1c: Form each letter from the chart.
l2c: Pause between letters. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l3c: Ask someone with the chart to say the name back.
safety: Use a fingerspelling chart. This is not a claim of fluency in a sign language.

name: Read one braille cell
description: Learn one braille cell from a reference and find it again by touch or by sight.
l1c: Match one letter to its dot pattern from a reference.
l2c: Find that pattern among three you can see or feel.
l3c: Say that one cell is not reading.
safety: Do not present this as literacy. Use a reference you may touch.

name: Add two numbers on an abacus
description: Add two small numbers on an abacus and check the sum in writing.
l1c: Set the first number and say it.
l2c: Add the second number on the abacus.
l3c: Write the sum and compare it with the abacus.
safety: Use a real or drawn abacus. Show the place values you are using.

name: Link items in a story
description: Remember eight ordinary items by linking them in one story, then recall them without the list.
l1c: Tell a story that includes the eight items in order.
l2c: Recall the eight without looking, and mark a miss.
l3c: Put the missed item back into the story and recall that part.
safety: Use harmless objects. This is a linking story, not the route method.

name: Redraw a pattern from memory
description: Look at a short pattern, cover it, and redraw it.
l1c: Look at a pattern of up to six marks.
l2c: Cover it and redraw it. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l3c: Uncover and mark what differed.
safety: Use your own drawing.

name: Peg three items to three pictures
description: Attach three items to three fixed pictures and recall the items from the pictures.
l1c: Choose three pictures you will reuse.
l2c: Link one item to each picture with a vivid pair.
l3c: Look at the pictures and say the items.
l3d: You can recall from the pegs.
safety: Use ordinary items.

name: Tie a bow that survives a tug
description: Tie a gift bow and tug the loops without it coming undone.
l1c: Tie a bow with two loops.
l2c: Tug each loop once and say whether it held.
l3c: If it slips, retie it and tug again.
safety: Use ribbon or cloth, not around a neck.

name: Fold a napkin so it stands
description: Fold a napkin into a shape that stands on a table.
l1c: Fold one standing shape.
l2c: Stand it and take your hands away.
l3c: Unfold it so it can still be used as a napkin.
l3d: You can return it to use.
safety: Use a clean napkin.

name: Move a bean with chopsticks
description: Move one bean from one dish to another with chopsticks.
l1c: Pick up one bean and hold it.
l2c: Move it to the other dish without using the other hand on the bean.
l3c: Set it down where you aimed.
safety: Use chopsticks and a bean or a similar small food you may eat. Do not stab toward a hand.

name: Make a pom-pom that holds
description: Make a yarn pom-pom and show it holds together when you shake it.
l1c: Wrap yarn and tie the middle.
l2c: Cut the loops and fluff it.
l3c: Shake it once and say whether yarn fell out.
safety: Cut away from fingers. Keep yarn away from pets and babies.

name: Finger-knit a cord
description: Finger-knit a short cord and pull it so the stitches stay.
l1c: Make the first stitches on your fingers.
l2c: Knit a length you can hold up.
l3c: Pull the working yarn and show the cord does not unravel at the tied end.
safety: Use yarn. Do not pull against a finger joint.

name: Stitch a cross-stitch row
description: Sew a short row of cross-stitches that all cross the same way.
l1c: Sew one X. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l2c: Sew several crosses in a row.
l3c: Point to the direction of the top stitch on each, and fix one that differs.
safety: Use a needle on scrap cloth. Do not sew toward a hand.

name: Bead a repeating pattern
description: String a bead pattern of three colors that repeats, and read the pattern back.
l1c: Write the three-color order.
l2c: String at least two repeats.
l3c: Read the colors aloud and stop at a mistake.
safety: Use beads you may handle. Keep them away from small children.

name: Braid a short lanyard
description: Braid a short lanyard from three strands and tug the end.
l1c: Start three strands and make the first crosses.
l2c: Braid a length you can wear as a loop or hold up.
l3c: Tie or fuse the end as the material allows and tug it.
safety: Use cord or yarn. Do not melt plastic if you do not know the material. A knot is enough.

name: Wrap a yarn diamond
description: Wrap yarn around two sticks so a diamond pattern shows.
l1c: Tie the sticks in a cross.
l2c: Wrap one color so the diamond starts.
l3c: Add a second color and point to the edge between them.
safety: Use craft sticks and yarn. This is a yarn craft, not a ceremonial object.

name: Sew a blanket stitch
description: Sew a short blanket stitch along the edge of scrap cloth.
l1c: Make the first loop on the edge.
l2c: Sew several stitches that look alike.
l3c: Point to one loop and say what it holds.
safety: Use a needle on scrap. Do not sew cloth someone is wearing.

name: Make a tassel
description: Make a tassel, bind the head, and show the skirt hanging.
l1c: Cut or wrap a bundle. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l2c: Tie the head so the skirt hangs.
l3c: Trim the ends so they hang together, or say you left them uneven on purpose.
safety: Cut away from fingers.

name: Spool-knit a few rounds
description: Knit a few rounds on a spool or a fork and pull the cord through.
l1c: Set the loops on the pegs.
l2c: Knit several rounds. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l3c: Pull the cord out and show the tube.
safety: Keep the tool away from eyes.

name: Make a corner bookmark
description: Make a corner bookmark and fit it on a page.
l1c: Make the pocket that takes a page corner.
l2c: Put it on a page corner.
l3c: Turn the page and show the bookmark stayed or say it slipped.
safety: Use a book you may mark, or a scrap page.

name: Erase a pencil line without a tear
description: Erase a pencil line and show the paper still whole.
l1c: Draw one pencil line on scrap.
l2c: Erase it until the line is gone or a ghost remains.
l3c: Show that the paper did not tear.
safety: Use scrap paper and a pencil.

name: Sharpen a pencil to a point
description: Sharpen a pencil until it writes a fine line.
l1c: Use a sharpener you can hold safely.
l2c: Write one fine line. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l2d: You can write with the point.
l3c: Stop before the lead breaks back to a stub, or say it broke and resharpen.
safety: Keep fingers out of the blade. Do not use a knife.

name: Draw parallel lines with a guide
description: Draw two lines that stay the same distance apart.
l1c: Draw one straight line with a guide.
l2c: Draw a second line and measure the gap at both ends.
l3c: Say whether the lines would meet if extended, from the two measures.
safety: Use a ruler on paper.

name: Draw a circle with string
description: Draw a circle with a pin or a held center and a string, and mark the center.
l1c: Mark the point the string turns around.
l2c: Draw the circle with the string kept tight.
l3c: Measure from the center to the line in two places and say if they match.
safety: If you use a pin, keep it in the table or a board, not in a hand.

name: Fold a right angle
description: Fold a paper right angle and test it against a corner you trust.
l1c: Fold a straight edge onto itself to make a right angle.
l2c: Hold it against a known square corner.
l3c: Say whether it matched or where it gaped.
safety: Use paper.

name: Check a square with a 3-4-5 string
description: Lay a 3-4-5 string triangle and say whether a drawn corner matches the right angle.
l1c: Mark the three lengths on string or tape.
l2c: Lay it so the right angle sits on the corner you are checking.
l3c: Say whether the corner matches, or that the string slipped.
safety: Use string on a flat drawing, not on a roof or a live wire.

name: Center a frame on a page
description: Place a rectangle so the margins on the left and right match.
l1c: Put the rectangle on the page.
l2c: Write the two side margins.
l3c: Move it until the two margins match, or say how far off you left it.
safety: Use paper.

name: Cut a window in card
description: Cut a window in card so a picture shows through and the border stays in one piece.
l1c: Draw the window smaller than the card.
l2c: Cut the window out. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l3c: Lay a picture behind it and say whether the border covers the edge.
safety: Cut away from fingers. Use card, not glass.

name: Hinge a photo on a page
description: Attach a photo or a scrap print with a hinge so you can lift it.
l1c: Fasten only one edge. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l2c: Lift the photo and lay it back.
l3c: Show that the face has no adhesive on the picture.
safety: Use a scrap print or a photo you may hinge.

name: Label the back of a print
description: Write a date and a short title on the back of a print with a pencil.
l1c: Show the back. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l2c: Write the date and a few words lightly.
l3c: Look at the face and say whether the writing dented it.
safety: Use pencil, not a pen that bleeds. Use a print you may write on.

name: Deal a fan of cards
description: Spread a small fan of cards so each corner shows.
l1c: Start from a squared deck.
l2c: Spread a fan in one hand or on the table.
l3c: Close it back into a square.
safety: Use cards you may handle.

name: Shuffle a small deck overhand
description: Shuffle a small deck with an overhand shuffle and square it.
l1c: Move packets from one hand to the other.
l2c: Square the deck so no card sticks out.
l3c: Deal five cards and say whether they stuck together.
l3d: You can deal after the shuffle.
safety: Use your own cards. Do not present the shuffle as a way to cheat.

name: Deal into two even piles
description: Deal a small even deck into two piles with the same count.
l1c: Count the cards before you deal.
l2c: Deal one to each pile until the deck is gone.
l3c: Count both piles and say they match, or where you misdealt.
safety: Use a small deck.

name: Float a paperclip
description: Float a dry paperclip on water and say what happens when you touch the surface.
l1c: Lay the clip on the water so it stays up.
l2c: Touch the water and say whether the clip sank.
l3c: Dry the clip and try again, or say the water is now disturbed.
safety: Use a cup of water and a clip. Do not drink the water.

name: Separate ink on paper
description: Put a water-based dot on paper, let water creep through it, and say what colors you see.
l1c: Put one dot above the water line.
l2c: Let water climb the paper and stop before the dot runs off the top.
l3c: Name the colors you see, or say you see only one.
safety: Use water-based ink, not a solvent. Do not taste it.

name: Pick up a clip with a nail coil
description: Wrap wire around a nail, connect a battery briefly, and see whether the nail picks up a clip.
l1c: Wrap insulated or carefully handled wire around the nail.
l2c: Touch the battery and try to lift one clip, then disconnect.
l3c: Say whether the clip dropped when you disconnected, and stop if anything feels warm.
safety: Use one small battery. Disconnect at once if the wire or battery feels warm. Do not use a wall outlet. Do not leave it connected.

name: Reveal a lemon line with a lamp
description: Write with lemon juice, let it dry, and warm it with a lamp until the line shows or you stop.
l1c: Write one line and let it dry.
l2c: Hold the paper near a lamp, not a flame, and watch.
l3c: Stop when the line shows or when the paper smells hot, and say which.
safety: Do not use a flame, an oven, or an iron. Stop if the paper scorches.

name: See an upside-down view through a pinhole
description: Make a pinhole in a card and describe the upside-down view of a lamp or a window.
l1c: Prick one small hole. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l2c: Look at a lamp or a bright window through a simple pinhole setup and say what is upside down.
l3c: Say what you cannot tell from that view.
safety: Do not look at the sun. Prick the card away from your hand.

name: Align two mirrors to see behind you
description: Hold two mirrors so you can see something behind you.
l1c: Point to what one mirror shows.
l2c: Angle the second so you see behind you.
l3c: Name the object behind you that you could not see directly.
safety: Use unbreakable mirrors if you have them. Do not walk while looking only in the mirrors.

name: Make a rainbow with a glass and a lamp
description: Use a glass of water and a lamp to cast a colored patch, and point to the colors you see.
l1c: Aim a lamp, not the sun, through or past the glass.
l2c: Point to a colored patch on a wall or paper.
l3c: Name one color you can see in it.
safety: Do not use the sun. Do not look into the lamp.

name: Tune three bottles
description: Tune three bottles to three notes you can tell apart and play them in an order.
l1c: Make a note on each bottle.
l2c: Play them and say which is highest.
l3c: Play an order you said in advance.
safety: Do not share mouthpieces.

name: Strum a rubber-band box
description: Stretch bands over a box and play two different notes.
l1c: Put at least two bands on a box.
l2c: Pluck two bands and say which is higher.
l3c: Tighten or shorten one band and say what the note did.
safety: Do not aim a band at anyone.

name: Find the full glass by sound
description: Tap glasses with different amounts of water and say which sounds lower.
l1c: Fill them to two different levels.
l2c: Tap each and say which sounds lower.
l3c: Look at the levels and say whether your ear matched the fuller glass.
safety: Tap gently. Use glasses you may handle.

name: Finish a tangram outline
description: Fill a tangram outline with the pieces, without looking at a solution picture.
l1c: Lay out the set. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l2c: Cover the outline without overlaps you ignore.
l3c: If you stop, name one piece that does not fit yet.
l3d: You can say where you are stuck.
safety: Use your own puzzle.

name: Solve a rebus
description: Solve a rebus from the pictures and say the phrase.
l1c: Say what each picture shows.
l2c: Say the phrase you think they make.
l3c: Check against the answer or say you have no key.
safety: Use a rebus you may solve. Do not use a rude one.

name: Move one match in a figure
description: Move one match in a drawn or stick figure so the figure matches the goal you stated.
l1c: Write what the figure should become.
l2c: Move only one match or stick.
l3c: Say whether the goal is met.
safety: Use sticks or drawn matches, not a flame.

name: Fill a small nonogram
description: Fill a small picture grid from the numbers, and check the row clues.
l1c: Complete one row from its clue.
l2c: Complete the small grid.
l3c: Check one column against its clue and fix it if needed.
safety: Use a puzzle you may mark.

name: Draw a maze and time a friend
description: Draw a maze with one path and time someone from the start to the end.
l1c: Draw a maze you can solve.
l2c: Time a person from start to end without pointing unless they ask.
l3c: After they finish or stop, show one wrong turn.
l3d: You can show a wrong turn.
safety: Use paper.

name: Write a palindrome
description: Write a short palindrome and show it reads the same backward.
l1c: Write a word or a short line.
l2c: Read it backward letter by letter.
l3c: If it fails, mark the letter that breaks it and fix the line or say you stopped.
safety: Keep it kind.

name: Solve a two-move slider
description: Solve a tiny sliding puzzle that needs only a few moves, and count the moves you used.
l1c: Say what the goal looks like.
l2c: Slide until you reach it.
l3c: Say how many slides you used.
safety: Use a physical or drawn slider.

name: Find a heavier ball
description: Use a balance twice at most to find which of three balls is heavier, if you know one is.
l1c: Weigh two balls against each other.
l2c: Say which is heavier from that weighing, or weigh the third if they balanced.
l3c: Check on the balance and say whether you were right.
safety: Use safe balls and a balance, not a guess about a person.

name: Read a measuring cup at eye level
description: Read a line on a measuring cup with your eye level with the line.
l1c: Put the cup on a flat surface.
l2c: Crouch or lift the cup so your eye is at the line and read it.
l3c: Say what you would misread if you looked from above.
safety: Use water. Do not use a hot liquid.

name: Tare a scale
description: Put a container on a scale, tare it, and weigh one thing inside it.
l1c: Zero the scale with the empty container on it.
l2c: Add one item and read the number.
l3c: Remove the item and say whether the scale returns to zero.
safety: Use a kitchen scale and a safe item.

name: Check a scale with a known weight
description: Weigh an object whose weight is printed and say whether the scale agrees.
l1c: Write the weight from the package or the object.
l2c: Weigh it and write the scale number.
l3c: Say whether they agree closely enough for your use.
safety: Do not open a sealed package if you should not.

name: Carry a tray on one hand
description: Carry a light tray on one flat hand across a short distance.
l1c: Hold the tray level with one empty cup on it.
l2c: Walk a few steps. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l3c: Set it down without a slide you ignore.
safety: Use plastic. Do not load it with hot liquid.

name: Peel in one strip
description: Peel an orange or a similar fruit in one strip if the peel allows, or say where it broke.
l1c: Start one continuous strip.
l2c: Peel as far as the strip holds.
l3c: Show the strip and the point it broke, or the whole peel.
safety: Use fruit you may eat. Wash it. Stop if a knife is needed.

name: Open a jar with a better grip
description: Open a jar you are allowed to open, using a cloth or a grip, and say what worked.
l1c: Try the lid and say whether it moved.
l2c: Use a dry cloth or a gripper and try again.
l3c: Say whether it opened, and leave a stuck jar for someone else rather than forcing a glass lip.
safety: Do not strike glass. Do not use heat. Do not open a jar that is not yours.

name: Sort buttons by holes
description: Sort a handful of buttons by the number of holes.
l1c: Label piles for the hole counts you actually see.
l2c: Put each button in a pile.
l3c: Put a button aside if the holes are unclear.
safety: Use buttons, not a sewing project someone needs undisturbed.

name: Sort coins by the year you can read
description: Sort coins into decades or years you can actually read, and set aside worn ones.
l1c: Read one year aloud. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l2c: Sort the readable coins.
l3c: Put coins with unreadable years in a separate pile.
safety: Use ordinary coins. Do not clean them with a chemical.

name: Sort stones by one feature
description: Sort a few stones by one feature you name before you start.
l1c: Write the one feature, such as rough or smooth.
l2c: Sort the stones by that feature only.
l3c: Point to one stone that could go either way.
l3d: You can see a border case.
safety: Do not take stones from a protected place.

name: Match a key to an outline
description: Draw the outline of a key and match the key back to that drawing among two outlines.
l1c: Draw one key's outline. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l2c: Draw or place a second different outline.
l3c: Match the key to the right outline without looking at a label.
safety: Use keys you may draw. Do not copy a key.

name: Tell two screws apart by the thread
description: Tell two screws apart by the thread you can see, not only by the head.
l1c: Point to the threads on each.
l2c: Say one difference, such as fine or coarse, or that you cannot tell.
l3c: Place a third screw with the one it matches, or set it aside.
safety: Do not force a screw into a hole.

name: Tell a knit from a woven cloth
description: Tell a knit cloth from a woven cloth by the structure you can see or stretch.
l1c: Point to the loops or the crossed threads.
l1d: You can look at the structure.
l2c: Stretch gently and say which one springs back more.
l3c: Name which is knit and which is woven, or say you are not sure.
safety: Use cloth you may handle. Do not burn a fiber.

name: Read a boarding pass
description: Find the gate, the seat, and the boarding time on a pass or a sample.
l1c: Point to the seat. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l2c: Point to the gate, or say the pass does not show one yet.
l2d: You can look for the gate.
l3c: Point to the boarding time and say what it is not, such as arrival.
l3d: You can tell the times apart.
safety: Use your own pass or a sample. Do not share a document that shows a private number you do not need.

name: Find a seat from a row number
description: Find a seat from a row and a letter in a room, a vehicle, or a drawing.
l1c: Read the row and the letter.
l2c: Stand at that seat or point to it on a plan.
l3c: Say who or what is on one side, from the labels.
safety: Do not sit in a seat assigned to someone else.

name: Set a lock to a code you wrote
description: Set a combination lock to a code you wrote down, then open it from the note.
l1c: Write the code before you scramble the lock.
l2c: Scramble it and open it using the note.
l2d: You can open it from the note.
l3c: Say where you will keep the note, not on the bag in plain sight if the bag is public.
safety: Use your own lock. Do not lock anyone's bag as a joke.

name: Read a queue ticket
description: Read a queue number and say how you will know when it is your turn.
l1c: Read the number on the ticket.
l2c: Point to the display or the board that calls numbers.
l3c: Say how many numbers are between the display and yours, or that you cannot see the display.
safety: Use a real ticket or a sample. Do not skip a queue.

name: Read a locker label
description: Match a locker number to a key or a ticket.
l1c: Read the number on the key or the ticket.
l2c: Find the matching door. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l3c: If it does not open, stop and say you will ask, rather than forcing it.
safety: Use your own locker or a labeled practice door. Do not force a lock.

name: Note the car you boarded
description: Note the car or carriage you entered so you can find an exit or a companion.
l1c: Read the letter or number on the car.
l2c: Write it down or say it to the person you are with.
l3c: From the platform side or a note, point back to that mark.
safety: Do not block a door.

name: Explain a trick after you show it
description: Show one small trick you can do, then explain the method to the person who watched.
l1c: Do the trick once. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l2c: Explain the method in a few sentences.
l3c: Let them try the method, or show the one move they missed.
safety: Explain only a trick of your own. Do not use it to take something.

name: Film your hands so the move shows
description: Film your hands doing one move so a viewer can see the move.
l1c: Film so both hands stay in view.
l2c: Do one move once. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l2d: You can do it on camera.
l3c: Watch the clip and say whether the move is visible.
safety: Film your own hands. Do not include a person who declined.

name: Bow and stop
description: End a short trick with a bow or a nod and do not add another trick.
l1c: Complete the one trick you announced.
l2c: Give one clear ending. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l3c: Do not start a second trick unless they ask.
safety: Keep the ending short.

name: Teach a one-minute trick
description: Teach a trick that takes about a minute, and watch the learner do it.
l1c: Show the moves in order.
l2c: Watch them do it without taking the object back unless they ask.
l3c: Name one thing to change, or say it worked.
safety: Teach a harmless trick.

name: Roll a hoop and catch it
description: Roll a hoop in a straight line and catch it before it falls.
l1c: Roll the hoop so it stays up.
l2c: Catch it while it is still upright.
l3c: Say whether it rolled straight.
safety: Use an open space away from people and roads.

name: Turn a hoop at your waist
description: Keep a hoop turning around your waist for several turns.
l1c: Get the hoop turning. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l2c: Keep it up for several turns a watcher can count.
l3c: Catch the hoop as it drops.
safety: Use a hoop in an open space. Stop if you feel dizzy.

name: Spin a ball on a finger
description: Spin a ball on one finger and catch it.
l1c: Get the ball turning on the finger.
l2c: Keep it up long enough to see.
l3c: Catch it when it tips. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
safety: Use a ball you can control. Spin it away from faces.

name: Cross a jump rope once
description: Jump a rope with one jump, then cross the arms for one jump and uncross.
l1c: Jump one plain jump. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l2c: Cross the arms for one jump.
l3c: Return to a plain jump. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
safety: Use a rope on a clear floor. Stop if you catch a foot and rest.

name: Flip a card cleanly
description: Flip one card from face down to face up without sending it off the table.
l1c: Place one card face down.
l2c: Flip it face up on the table.
l3c: Show it stayed on the table.
safety: Use a card and a clear table.

name: Separate two paper rings
description: Make two paper rings that look linked and show whether they are, by the cut you planned.
l1c: Make two rings in the setup you chose.
l2c: Pull them and say whether they separate.
l3c: Show the cut or the slit that decides it.
safety: Use paper strips.

name: Build a card bridge
description: Bridge a small gap with cards so a coin can sit on it, or say the gap is too wide.
l1c: Set the cards across a small gap.
l2c: Set one coin on the bridge.
l3c: Say a wider gap you would not try.
safety: Use cards and a coin. Do not stand on the bridge.

name: Balance a fork and explain it
description: Balance a fork and spoon or a fork on a glass using a match or a toothpick setup you can explain.
l1c: Put the pieces together.
l2c: Set it on the glass so it stays.
l3c: Point to where the weight sits.
safety: Use unbreakable stand-ins if the glass is risky. Do not light a match. Keep hands clear of a glass rim that could break.

name: Referee a coin flip
description: Flip a coin where both people can see it, and call the result only after it lands.
l1c: Show both faces before the flip.
l2c: Let it land on a surface, not on a hand you cover.
l3c: Call the face only after it has landed, and show it.
safety: Do not use this to settle something that needs a real decision process. It is a fair flip, not a judge.

name: Read opposite faces on a die
description: Say which faces are opposite on a standard die you can check.
l1c: Name one pair of opposite faces.
l2c: Look at the die and say whether that pair is opposite.
l3c: From a face you see, say the hidden opposite.
safety: Use a die you can turn. Do not claim a die is fair from this.

name: Pour to a marked line
description: Pour water to a marked line and stop at the line.
l1c: Point to the line before you pour.
l2c: Pour and stop at the line, at eye level.
l2d: You can stop at the line.
l3c: Say whether you passed the line and how you would correct it.
safety: Use water in a stable jug.

name: Make a compass rose you can turn
description: Draw a compass rose, label the four directions, and turn it to match a known north.
l1c: Write north, east, south, and west.
l2c: Turn the paper so north matches a north you were given or a compass you may use.
l3c: Name what lies to the east of you on that orientation.
safety: If you use a compass, follow its simple use. Do not treat a drawing as a compass by itself.

name: Copy a rhythm you just heard
description: Hear a short clapped rhythm and clap it back.
l1c: Listen once without clapping along.
l2c: Clap the rhythm back. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l3c: Ask whether it matched, and fix one hit if it did not.
safety: Use a short rhythm. Keep the volume kind.

name: Make a note on a straw
description: Cut a straw end, blow one note, and shorten it to change the note.
l1c: Blow one note on the cut straw.
l2c: Shorten it and say whether the note moved.
l3c: Say which length was easier.
safety: Cut away from fingers. Do not share the straw.

name: Roll a cloth strip
description: Roll a cloth strip into a tight roll that stays when you set it down.
l1c: Start a tight end. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l2c: Roll the strip. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l3c: Set it down and say whether it unrolled.
l3d: You can see if it stays.
safety: This is rolling cloth, not first aid. Do not apply it to a person.

name: Fold a cloth into a triangle
description: Fold a square cloth into a triangle that stays folded.
l1c: Fold the square in half into a triangle.
l1d: You can make the first fold.
l2c: Fold it into a smaller triangle.
l3c: Show the edges that line up, or the one that does not.
safety: Use a cloth you may fold.

name: Thread a belt
description: Thread a belt through the loops so it sits flat and the end goes through the buckle.
l1c: Start the end at the buckle side.
l2c: Pass every loop. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l3c: Fasten it and show the end held.
safety: Use a belt on clothing you may adjust, or on a held pair of loops.

name: Tie a bow on a package
description: Tie a bow on a wrapped package so the knot sits in the middle of one face.
l1c: Put the knot where you want it.
l2c: Tie the bow. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l3c: Turn it and say whether the bow stayed centered.
safety: Use a package you may tie.

name: Stack dice to a sum you named
description: Stack dice so the top faces add to a sum you wrote before you started.
l1c: Write a small sum you can reach.
l2c: Stack dice to reach it. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l3c: Read the top faces and say the total.
safety: Use dice on a table.

name: Invent a harmless code
description: Invent a code for five letters, write the key, and decode a word with it.
l1c: Write five letters and their signs.
l2c: Encode one word. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l3c: Decode it from the key without looking at the word.
safety: Do not use the code to hide something from a person who needs to understand you.

name: Read the digits under a barcode
description: Read the digits printed under a barcode and find them again on a second look.
l1c: Read the digits aloud. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l2c: Look away and write them.
l2d: You can recall a short run.
l3c: Check against the package and mark a wrong digit.
safety: Use a package you may handle. The digits are not a price.

name: Spot a repeated bead in a string
description: Find a color that repeats too soon in a bead string you made or were given.
l1c: Say the pattern you expect.
l2c: Point to the bead that breaks it.
l3c: Fix it if the string is yours, or mark it if it is not.
safety: Use beads, not jewelry you must not alter.

name: Make a paper pocket
description: Fold a paper pocket that holds a card.
l1c: Fold a pocket with one open side.
l2c: Slide a card inside. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l3c: Turn it over and say whether the card fell.
safety: Use paper and a card.

name: Trace a coin and fit it
description: Trace a coin and fit the same coin back into the circle.
l1c: Trace one coin. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l2c: Fit that coin into the circle.
l3c: Try a different coin and say whether it fits.
l3d: You can tell two coins apart.
safety: Use coins you may trace.

name: Clap the syllables and stop
description: Clap the syllables of a word and stop when the word ends.
l1c: Clap one clap for each syllable.
l2c: Stop when the word ends, with no extra clap.
l3c: Clap a second word and say which had more syllables.
safety: This is syllable clapping, not a claim about stress.

name: Hum a note and stop on a sign
description: Hum one note and stop when a partner raises a hand.
l1c: Hum one steady note. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l2c: Watch for the sign. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l3c: Stop when the hand goes up.
l3d: You can stop on the sign.
safety: Do not strain the voice.

name: Pass a cup behind your back
description: Pass a plastic cup from one hand to the other behind your back without a drop.
l1c: Move the cup behind you into the other hand.
l2c: Bring it forward still upright.
l3c: Say whether it stayed upright.
safety: Use an empty plastic cup.

name: Balance a spoon on your nose
description: Balance a light spoon on your nose for a moment, or say it slid.
l1c: Place the spoon and let go.
l2c: Hold still long enough to be seen.
l3c: Catch it when it slides.
safety: Use a clean light spoon. Do not use a sharp object. Stop if it hurts.

name: Name the fold that changed a dart
description: Fold a paper dart, change one named fold, and say what the flight did.
l1c: Fly it once and mark the landing.
l2c: Change one fold and name it before you throw again.
l3c: Say whether the second flight went farther or straighter.
safety: Fly where you will not hit anyone. This is one named change, not a new plane each time.

name: Tie a knot you can release
description: Tie a slipped knot around a rail or a bag handle and release it by pulling the free end.
l1c: Tie a knot with a loop you can pull, around something fixed.
l2c: Tug the standing part and show the knot holds.
l3c: Pull the free end and show the knot opens.
safety: Use cord on a rail, a chair, or a bag. Do not tie it around a person or a neck.

name: Spot a knot that will slip
description: Compare two tied cords and say which knot slips when you pull the free end.
l1c: Tie one firm knot and one slipped knot on scrap cord.
l2c: Pull each free end and say which opened.
l3c: Say which one you would use if you needed to undo it quickly.
safety: Use scrap cord, not a load that could fall on you.

name: Put a key on a ring
description: Open a split ring and put one key on it, then show the key stays.
l1c: Start the key onto the split.
l2c: Slide the key fully onto the ring.
l3c: Tug the key and show it does not come off.
safety: Use your own key. Do not pry the ring toward a hand or an eye.

name: Untangle a chain
description: Untangle a light chain and lay it in one line.
l1c: Find one end of the chain.
l2c: Open one loop without pulling a kink tighter.
l3c: Lay the chain in one line, or say which kink remains.
safety: Use a light chain. Do not force a knot that starts to kink the metal.

name: Gather a cloth edge
description: Sew a running stitch on scrap and pull it so the edge gathers.
l1c: Sew a loose running stitch along an edge.
l2c: Pull the thread so the cloth gathers.
l3c: Slide the gathers so they are not all in one lump.
safety: Use a needle on scrap cloth.

name: Run a cord through a casing
description: Run a cord through a fabric or paper channel and show both ends.
l1c: Use a folded channel you can open at the ends.
l2c: Push or pull the cord through.
l3c: Show an end sticking out of each side.
l3d: You can prove it went through.
safety: Use cord and scrap. Do not use a cord around a neck.

name: Pin a temporary hem
description: Pin a hem so it holds for a try-on and can be removed without a tear.
l1c: Fold the edge to the length you want.
l2c: Pin it so the pins stay on the inside.
l3c: Take the pins out and show the cloth is not torn.
safety: Point pins away from the body. Do not wear the cloth while you pin if you can pin it flat.

name: Roll a tie for a bag
description: Roll a necktie so it does not crease into a hard fold, and unroll it.
l1c: Roll from the narrow end.
l2c: Put it in a bag and take it out.
l3c: Unroll it and say whether a hard crease appeared.
safety: Use a tie you may roll.

name: Tie a scarf so it stays
description: Tie a scarf with one knot and turn your head without it falling.
l1c: Use one knot, not a stack of them.
l2c: Turn your head both ways.
l3c: If it slips, retie it once and test again.
safety: Do not tie it tightly around the neck.

name: Button a cuff
description: Button a cuff, or a spare cuff, with the hand that has to reach it.
l1c: Hold the button and the hole.
l2c: Pass the button through the hole.
l3c: Undo it without pulling the thread.
safety: Stop if a button is loose. Do not pull it off.

name: Fold a towel that stacks
description: Fold a towel into a rectangle and stack a second fold on it so the edges match.
l1c: Fold one towel into a rectangle.
l2c: Fold a second the same way and stack it.
l3c: Say whether the edges match.
safety: Use towels you may fold.

name: Hang trousers so the creases match
description: Hang trousers so the legs lie together and the waist is supported.
l1c: Lay the inner seams together.
l2c: Put them on a bar or a hanger.
l3c: Say whether the hems hang level.
safety: Use trousers you may hang.

name: Fold a cube from a net
description: Cut or use a cube net, fold it, and show a closed cube.
l1c: Count the six faces before you fold.
l2c: Fold it into a cube. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l3c: Tuck the last face and show it stays, or say which tab failed.
safety: Cut away from fingers if you cut the net.

name: Reject a net that will not fold
description: Look at two cube nets and say which one will not fold into a closed cube, then test with paper.
l1c: Point to the net you think will fail.
l2c: Fold both, or fold the one you rejected.
l3c: Say whether your choice was right.
safety: Use paper nets.

name: Find the center with diagonals
description: Draw both diagonals of a rectangle and mark where they cross.
l1c: Draw one corner-to-corner line.
l2c: Draw the second diagonal.
l3c: Mark the crossing and check it is inside the rectangle.
safety: Use a drawn rectangle.

name: Mark a vertical with string
description: Hang a string with a small weight and mark a vertical line beside it.
l1c: Hang it so the weight can rest still.
l2c: Wait until it stops swinging.
l3c: Mark a line beside the string and say it is vertical only while the string hangs free.
safety: Use a light weight that cannot hurt a foot. Do not hang it where someone walks into it.

name: Draw a viewfinder
description: Cut a small rectangle and use it to choose a view before you draw or photograph.
l1c: Cut a small window in card.
l2c: Hold it up and name what is inside.
l3c: Draw or photograph that view and say what you left out.
safety: Cut away from fingers. Do not block a path while you look.

name: Fill the frame with a texture
description: Take a photo where a texture fills the frame, with no horizon.
l1c: Point to the texture before you shoot.
l2c: Take the photo so the texture goes to the edges.
l3c: Look at the photo and say whether an edge of the object shows.
safety: Photograph a thing, not a person who declined.

name: Make a silhouette
description: Place a lamp so a profile becomes a dark shape on a wall, and trace it if you may.
l1c: Put the lamp so the shadow edge is clear.
l2c: Point to the nose and the chin in the shadow.
l3c: Trace it on paper if you may, or say you only looked.
safety: Use a lamp, not a flame. Ask before you trace a person's profile.

name: Trace a profile
description: Trace a consenting person's profile or your own shadow, and show the line.
l1c: Ask them to hold still, or use your own shadow.
l2c: Trace the outline once. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l3c: Show the line and name one feature it caught.
safety: Ask before you trace a person. Use a lamp, not a flame.

name: Mime a heavy box
description: Pick up an imaginary box so a watcher can tell it is heavy.
l1c: Reach for the box with both hands.
l2c: Change your body so the weight reads.
l3c: Set it down and leave it there.
safety: Do not strain a real lift. This is mime.

name: Pass an imaginary object
description: Pass an imaginary object to a partner so they receive its size.
l1c: Shape the object in your hands.
l2c: Hand it over and let go.
l3c: See whether they keep the same size, and say what changed.
safety: Agree to play. Stop if they stop.

name: Hold a still pose
description: Hold a pose while someone walks around you, and say what moved.
l1c: Choose a pose you can hold.
l2c: Hold it while they walk to one side.
l3c: Name one thing that moved, or say you stayed still.
safety: Stop if a joint hurts. Do not hold your breath.

name: Hit a mark and turn
description: Walk to a mark on the floor, stop, and turn to a named direction.
l1c: Point to the mark before you walk.
l2c: Stop with a foot on the mark.
l3c: Turn to the direction you named.
safety: Use a mark on a clear floor.

name: Match steps with a partner
description: Walk beside a partner and match their step length for a short distance.
l1c: Start on the same step. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l2c: Walk beside them and keep the same pace.
l3c: Stop when they stop. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
safety: Agree the walk. Do not pull them.

name: Clap off the beat
description: Tap a steady beat with a foot and clap between the taps.
l1c: Tap a steady beat with a foot.
l1d: You can keep the foot beat.
l2c: Clap in the spaces. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l2d: You can clap off the beat.
l3c: Keep the foot going and stop the claps.
safety: Keep the volume kind.

name: Write a postcard that fits
description: Write a message that fits in the message area of a postcard and leave the address side clear.
l1c: Point to where the message goes.
l2c: Write a message that stays inside it.
l3c: Show the address side has no message on it.
l3d: You can keep the sides apart.
safety: Use a card you may write on. Do not write a private address you should not share.

name: See if a letter is under a limit
description: Weigh a letter and say whether it is under a limit you wrote down first.
l1c: Write the limit before you weigh.
l2c: Weigh the letter and write the number.
l3c: Say whether it is under the limit.
safety: Use a scale and a letter you may weigh.

name: Roll a towel for a bag
description: Roll a towel tightly enough that it stays rolled in a bag.
l1c: Roll the towel from one end.
l2c: Put it in a bag and take it out.
l3c: Say whether it stayed rolled.
safety: Use a towel you may pack.

name: Make a box divider
description: Fold a divider that splits a box into two spaces a small object cannot cross.
l1c: Mark the width the divider must span.
l2c: Put it in so it stands. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l3c: Put a small object on one side and tip the box slightly.
safety: Use card and a box you may alter.

name: Label a jar so the tape peels
description: Label a jar with tape you can peel off without leaving the jar for someone else to scrape.
l1c: Write what is in the jar, or a practice word.
l2c: Stick it on the jar. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l3c: Peel it off and show the jar.
safety: Use a jar you may label. Do not label a jar of something you cannot identify.

name: Twist hair and pin it
description: Twist a section of hair, or a yarn stand-in, and pin it so it stays.
l1c: Twist the section. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l2c: Pin it so the pin lies flat.
l3c: Shake gently and say whether it stayed.
safety: Pin only hair you were asked to pin, or use yarn. Keep the pin point away from the scalp as you close it.

name: Tie a hair ribbon that stays
description: Tie a ribbon around a handle or a consenting ponytail so the bow survives a tug.
l1c: Tie a bow. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l2c: Tug the tails, not the hair.
l3c: Untie it without pulling hair.
safety: Ask before you tie anyone's hair. Do not tie it tightly.

name: Tape a costume hem
description: Tape a temporary hem that holds for a bow and peels off.
l1c: Tape the fold on the inside.
l2c: Bow or walk a few steps.
l3c: Peel the tape and show the cloth.
safety: Use tape on a costume you may alter. Do not tape skin.

name: Pin a cape so it releases
description: Pin a cloth at the shoulder with a safety pin you can undo quickly.
l1c: Pin two layers. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l2c: Turn once and say whether it held.
l3c: Undo the pin and show the cloth free.
safety: Keep the pin point closed. Do not pin skin.

name: Mark stage left from the stage
description: Stand on a practice stage and mark the side that is your left as you face the audience.
l1c: Face the side you are calling the audience.
l2c: Mark that side as stage left.
l3c: Walk to the audience side and say that their right is your left.
safety: Use a practice space, not a dark stage edge.

name: Mime a wall
description: Show an imaginary wall by touching it in three places a watcher can follow.
l1c: Touch one high point. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l2c: Touch two side points at the same distance.
l3c: Ask a watcher where the wall is.
safety: Do not push a real person.

name: Follow a partner's palm
description: Keep your palm a short distance from a partner's palm as they move.
l1c: Agree the gap. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l2c: Follow for a few moves without touching.
l3c: Stop when they stop. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
safety: Agree to play. Do not touch them.

name: Count a tempo aloud
description: Count a steady tempo aloud and stop on a number you chose.
l1c: Say the number you will stop on.
l2c: Count evenly up to it. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l3c: Stop on that number, not the next.
safety: Keep it quiet enough for the room.

name: Make a paper beard
description: Cut a paper beard, try it on, and take it off.
l1c: Cut a beard shape with a way to hold it.
l2c: Hold it in place. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l3c: Take it off and show it is one piece.
safety: Cut away from the face. Do not glue it to skin.

name: Release a gather
description: Gather scrap cloth and then let the thread go so the cloth lies flatter.
l1c: Pull a running stitch so the cloth gathers.
l2c: Ease the thread so the cloth flattens.
l3c: Show the gathered state and the released state, or say the thread broke.
safety: Use scrap and a needle.

name: Read a postage mark
description: Read a stamp or a printed postage mark and say what it does not tell you.
l1c: Point to the mark. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l2n: Read a value or a word
l2c: Read one word or value you can see.
l3c: Say one thing it does not tell you, such as the date it was posted if that is missing.
safety: Use a stamp or a sample you may handle.

name: Pack a cylinder so it does not roll
description: Pack a cylinder in a box so it does not roll when you tip the box a little.
l1c: Tip the loose cylinder and see it roll.
l2c: Add paper or a divider so it stays.
l3c: Tip the box a little and say whether it rolled.
safety: Use a light cylinder and a box.

name: Make a neck rest from a scarf
description: Roll a scarf into a rest you can put behind your neck and then unroll.
l1c: Roll the scarf. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l2c: Put it behind the neck and say whether it stays for a moment.
l3c: Unroll it so it is a scarf again.
safety: Do not wrap it around the neck as a support while you sleep. This is a short rest only.

name: Draw a hand as a simple shape
description: Draw a hand as a palm shape plus a thumb, and ask someone to point to the thumb.
l1c: Draw the palm as one shape.
l2c: Add the thumb where it joins.
l3c: Ask someone to point to the thumb.
safety: Use your own drawing.

name: Shade a circle so it looks round
description: Shade a circle with one side darker and say where the light is.
l1c: Say which side the light comes from.
l2c: Shade the opposite side darker.
l3c: Ask someone where the light is, from the drawing.
safety: Use pencil on paper.

name: Compare two prints you made
description: Make two prints of your own finger and say one way they match.
l1c: Ink or pencil-smudge your own finger twice on paper.
l2c: Point to one ridge or shape that appears in both.
l3c: Say you are not identifying a person beyond yourself.
safety: Use your own prints only. Do not take someone else's print. Wash your finger.

name: Fold a fitted sheet
description: Fold a fitted sheet into a rectangle you can stack, and say where a corner is tucked.
l1c: Tuck one elastic corner into another.
l2c: Fold it into a rectangle.
l3c: Point to the tucked corner in the finished fold.
safety: Use a sheet you may fold.

name: Center a title on a card
description: Write a title so the space on the left and the right looks even.
l1c: Write the title on scrap and mark its width.
l2c: Write or place it on the card with space on both sides.
l3c: Measure both side spaces and say whether they match.
safety: Use a card you may write on.

name: Make a paper accordion book
description: Fold a strip into an accordion and stand it so two pages show.
l1c: Fold the strip into even pages.
l2c: Stand it so it holds open.
l3c: Fold one page over and show the next.
safety: Use paper.

name: Read a platform letter
description: Read the platform or track mark on a sign and say which train side it names.
l1c: Point to the letter or number.
l2c: Say whether it names a platform, a track, or a car, from the words beside it.
l3c: If the sign does not say, write that you would ask.
l3d: You can stop when it is unclear.
safety: Use a sign or a sample. Do not cross a track.

name: Ask for a water refill
description: Ask for a refill of a bottle you already have, and stop if the answer is no.
l1c: Show the bottle you want filled.
l2c: Ask once, in a sentence.
l3c: If the answer is no, thank them and stop.
safety: Do not argue. Use a bottle you may fill.

name: Copy a short grid from memory
description: Look at a three-by-three grid of marks, cover it, and copy it.
l1c: Look at the grid long enough to try.
l2c: Cover it and copy the marks.
l3c: Uncover and mark one cell that differs, or say it matched.
safety: Use your own grid.

name: Teach a clap and stop the group
description: Teach two people a clap and stop them with a sign you agreed.
l1c: Agree the sign before you start.
l2c: Have them clap the pattern with you.
l3c: Give the sign and see them stop.
safety: Keep the volume kind.

name: Balance a card on a finger
description: Balance a card on one finger long enough to show, then catch it.
l1c: Rest the card and find a still point.
l2c: Hold it still long enough to be seen.
l3c: Catch the card when it tips.
safety: Use a card in an open space.

name: Spin a coin and trap it
description: Spin a coin on a table and trap it under a hand without sliding it off.
l1c: Spin the coin so it turns on edge.
l2c: Cover it while it is still moving.
l3c: Lift the hand and show the face that landed, without calling it early.
safety: Use a coin on a clear table.

name: Make a paper whistle
description: Fold a paper whistle, blow one note, and stop.
l1c: Fold a whistle that has a way for air to leave.
l2c: Produce one note. Leave the result where a watcher can see it.
l3c: Stop and flatten it, or say you will keep it.
safety: Use clean paper. Do not share the mouthpiece.
